candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — population health, risk-factor identification, screening/prevention planning, and health-promotion activities
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — population cancer surveillance used to target and evaluate prevention and screening programs
candidate.educational_objective: Apply population-based cancer registry data to health-promotion planning by using surveillance trends and disparities to guide and evaluate prevention, screening, and cancer-control efforts without substituting population statistics for individual clinical assessment.

options.A: Identify cancer trends and population groups with higher burden so prevention, screening, and cancer-control resources can be better targeted and evaluated.
options.B: Use the registry to determine with certainty which individual community members will develop cancer in the future.
options.C: Replace clinical screening recommendations for individual clients with population-level registry statistics alone.
options.D: Use the registry primarily to calculate hospital billing charges because cancer registry data have little public-health surveillance value.

candidate.rationale: CDC's National Program of Cancer Registries collects population-based information on new cancer cases, including cancer characteristics, initial treatment, and outcomes. Registry data are used to monitor cancer trends, identify patterns and higher-burden groups, guide planning and evaluation of cancer-control programs, help allocate health resources, and advance research. These population-level data support public-health planning but do not predict with certainty which individual will develop cancer and do not replace individualized screening recommendations.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CDC states that cancer registry data support monitoring trends, identifying population patterns and high-risk groups, planning and evaluating cancer-control programs, allocating resources, research, measuring prevention/control progress, identifying disparities, and improving outcomes.
